headline: Differences between PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments 'have eased'
subheadline: Bilawal’s inclusion in JCP significant in the context of PPP’s reported demand for greater say in judicial appointments
author: Ansar Abbasi
article_text:
Induction comes amid differences between two coalition partners.
Sources say differences between PPP and PML-N have eased.
Next meeting for JCP is scheduled this month on October 13.

ISLAMABAD: The induction of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Senator Rana Sanaullah into the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) comes amid recent differences between the two coalition partners over appointments to the superior judiciary, with sources suggesting that a fresh understanding could lead to reconsideration of PPP-backed candidates.

The two leaders were formally appointed members of the commission following the resignations of PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N member Sheikh Aftab Ahmad. Bilawal will represent the treasury benches in the National Assembly, while Rana Sanaullah will represent the Senate.

The appointments follow months of reported dissatisfaction within the PPP over its inability to secure the commission’s approval for several candidates it had supported for judicial positions.

According to media reports, Senator Farooq H Naek had proposed 33 candidates for appointments to the high courts: 16 for the Sindh High Court, 10 for the Lahore High Court, five for the Balochistan High Court and two for the Islamabad High Court. These reports said the PPP failed to secure approval for its preferred candidates in the relevant deliberations.

Sources familiar with the latest political discussions now suggest that differences between the PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments have eased. They believe the evolving understanding between the coalition partners could provide an opportunity for some PPP-backed candidates to be reconsidered in future rounds of appointments.

However, the extent of any such understanding, and whether it includes agreement on specific candidates, remains unclear. There is also no public confirmation of such an understanding by the two parties.

Bilawal’s inclusion in the commission is particularly significant in the context of the PPP’s reported demand for a greater say in judicial appointments. The party had previously expressed dissatisfaction after its preferred candidates failed to obtain the necessary support, while its senior legal representative, Farooq H Naek, had proposed candidates for several high courts. Apparently for the same reason, the Presidency had recently delayed approval of many appointments. The commission’s composition has become an important factor in the debate over judicial appointments following constitutional changes that expanded parliamentary representation in the process. Its decisions, however, continue to depend on the commission’s voting procedure.

The JCP’s next meeting is scheduled for October 13, 2026, with the extension of the term of the Sindh High Court’s constitutional benches on the reported agenda.

Originally published in The News

headline: Laiba Ijaz case: Suspect arrested from H-13; evidence of online fraud, blackmail emerges
subheadline: Gold medallist IIUI student allegedly died by suicide after discovering that her US university admission docs were fake
author: Ayaz Akbar Yousafzai, Azaz Syed, Duaa Mirza, Web Desk
article_text:
Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.
Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.
Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.

ISLAMABAD: A man suspected of supplying fake US university admission documents to International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) graduate Laiba Ijaz has been arrested from Islamabad’s H-13 sector, sources said.

Laiba reportedly died by suicide after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.

The suspect had rented a room in the area and was living in hiding, according to the sources.

They said investigators had also found evidence on his mobile phone of alleged online fraud and the blackmailing of women.

The suspect had previously worked in the Anti-Corruption Establishment in Quetta but was suspended, sources said. He had also worked for a company in Islamabad.

Laiba's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, within the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

According to police, she was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fraudulent.

Laiba's family said she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.

The family said an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university. Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.

The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.

When Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that they were fake, according to her family.

She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”

Police had said they were investigating the case from different angles and were awaiting Laiba’s post-mortem report to establish the cause of death.

PM Shehbaz takes notice

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.

The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.

He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.

Interior ministry orders FIA action

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.

He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.

The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.

FIA begins probe

The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.

Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.

He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.

According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.

Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.

The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.

headline: ATC disposes of Imaan, Hadi's plea against terrorism provisions in security breach case
subheadline: Islamabad court proceeded with the trial in couple's absence after their defence lawyers boycott proceedings
author: Arfa Feroz Zake
article_text:
Imaan, Hadi produced before court via video link.
ATC records three prosecution witnesses' statements.
Judge Sipra adjourns proceedings until Monday.

ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday disposed of a petition challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in a security breach case registered against lawyer and human rights activist Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha.

The case, registered at Aabpara Police Station, stems from allegations that the couple posed a security risk by interfering in state affairs during the visit of an international cricket team in October 2024.

The ATC in Islamabad indicted Mazari and Chattha in the case earlier this week despite the accused objecting that they had not yet received copies of the case documents.

During today's proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra questioned why the accused had not been produced before the court despite an order directing their appearance in person or through video link.

The judge directed court staff to contact Adiala jail authorities to establish why the two accused had not been brought to court. No jail official appeared before the court during the hearing.

The court subsequently sought a report from the jail authorities and briefly suspended proceedings to establish the circumstances surrounding the failure to produce the accused.

The couple was later produced via video link, where Chattha questioned why the two had not been produced before the court.

According to Chattha, they had learnt from newspaper reports the following day that charges had been framed against them in the case.

Judge Sipra responded that the accused had challenged the framing of charges, saying the high court would set aside the charge if it had not been framed correctly.

The judge also directed a jail official to submit an explanation for failing to produce Mazari and Chattha, saying the court had ordered their appearance.

The court disposed of an application challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in the case, with Judge Sipra saying the application could not be heard at the current stage of the proceedings.

The application was disposed of without hearing the defence lawyers.

Defence counsel Zainab Janjua said the accused had not been present before the court in person or via video link during the open-court proceedings.

Janjua alleged that Mazari and Chattha were being deprived of their right to a fair trial, and boycotted the proceedings along with the accused.

Following the boycott, the court proceeded with the trial in the absence of the couple and their defence lawyers, recording statements from three prosecution witnesses.

The court summoned further witnesses for Monday and adjourned the hearing until then.

Rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in custody since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them over a protest outside the Islamabad High Court.

A day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case related to controversial social media posts.

On September 17, following months of proceedings, the Supreme Court suspended the couple's sentences in a case related to controversial tweets and granted them bail against surety bonds worth Rs200,000 each, until the final decision on the case pending before the Islamabad High Court.

However, the relief was short-lived. Hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court (ATC).

According to the FIR, Mazari and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads during a protest.

headline: Federal govt decides to impose emergency in KP, sources say
subheadline: Cabinet to consider proposal tomorrow; separate National Assembly and Senate sessions to be held on Oct 13
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Cabinet meeting scheduled for Sunday morning: sources.
NA and Senate sessions to be summoned on Oct 13.
Section 144 imposed across Rawalpindi for one month.

The federal government has decided to impose an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march towards Islamabad, said well-informed sources on Saturday.

The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-e-Sadr.

The premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and others.

PPP’s Senator Sherry Rehman, Syed Naveed Qamar, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim Hussain were also present on the occasion.

“It was agreed in the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate on October 13,” read a statement issued by the President House.

The insiders said that the federal cabinet meeting sought for 9:30am on Sunday to approve emergency in KP.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz telephoned Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) Chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and congratulated him on performing Umrah.

The PM invited the JUI-F chief to a meeting at the Prime Minister’s House, which the latter accepted.

During the meeting, the JUI-F chief once again suggested to the premier to hold talks with PTI to end the ongoing political crisis in the country.

He suggested resolving the issue through negotiations rather than imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the insiders added.

He reiterated his support for meaningful talks between the government and the PTI to find a way forward.

The prime minister briefed the JUI-F chief in detail on the government’s efforts to engage in dialogue with the opposition.

PM Shehbaz said the government was making every possible effort to resolve the matter through mutual understanding, sources added.

The JUI-F chief urged the prime minister to take his party’s core committee into confidence over the matter.

He has sought more time from the PM to consult the opposition and PTI on resolving the ongoing political impasse, the sources added.

The JUI-F chief, later, contacted opposition leaders and the PTI leadership in Islamabad.

Federal cabinet to decide on KP emergency

Speaking on Geo News programme 'Naya Pakistan', KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said that no official decision has been taken on imposing an emergency or governor's rule in the province.

The governor said that said the federal cabinet would decide on Sunday whether to impose an emergency, governor's rule or both.

The governor also criticised KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying he should resign if he could not protect the people of his province.

Responding to a question, Kundi ruled out the possibility of further talks with the province's ruling party, the PTI.

The governor said several PTI members were either under arrest or surrendering themselves.

He alleged that the party did not want dialogue and questioned whether it could be considered a political party. Kundi further accused the PTI of engaging in talks only through confrontation and unrest.

No room left to avoid emergency: Naqvi

headline: Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, reaffirms commitment to Saudi security
subheadline: FO says targeting of civilian airport by Houthi militia constitutes heinous act of terrorism and grave threat to regional peace
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Islamabad urges world to condemn attacks on civilian infrastructure.
FO expresses concern over casualties, extends condolences to families.
Pakistan pledges continued support for Saudi security.

ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Sunday strongly condemned Houthi militia attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia and reaffirming Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.

At least 12 people were killed and 309 wounded in a Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, Saudi authorities said, as the Iran-backed group escalated its campaign against the kingdom.

The dead included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, according to the Saudi civil aviation authority.

In a statement, the prime minister condemned what he called a “heinous attack” and extended condolences to the bereaved families, while praying for the swift and full recovery of those injured.

“Attacks targeting civilians and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable and constitute a serious threat to regional peace and stability,” Shehbaz said, adding that such acts of violence, which constitute a flagrant violation of international law, must cease immediately.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with Saudi Arabia, its leadership and its people, citing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the enduring bonds of brotherhood between the two countries.

“We reaffirm our steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security,” the prime minister said.

Separately, the Foreign Office (FO) strongly condemned the latest terrorist attack by the Houthi militia, describing the targeting of a civilian airport as a heinous act of terrorism, a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to regional peace and security.

The FO expressed profound concern over reports of casualties and injuries resulting from the attack. It extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a swift and complete recovery, saying its prayers were with the victims and their families.

“The continued targeting of civilian population and critical infrastructure by the Houthi militia is utterly unacceptable and must be condemned unequivocally by the international community,” the FO said.

It added that such “brazen and indiscriminate acts of aggression” could not be justified under any circumstances and must cease immediately.

The Foreign Office said Pakistan stood in unwavering solidarity with the leadership and people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in the face of repeated terrorist attacks.

“In accordance with the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence and the recent decisions taken by its Strategic, Political and Defence Committee, Pakistan reiterates its firm and unshakeable commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the statement said.

The FO also said Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend its territory, protect its people and safeguard its cities and vital infrastructure against all threats and acts of aggression.

Calling for an immediate halt to the attacks, Pakistan urged the Houthi militia to cease its terrorist activities and called on the international community to take a firm and unequivocal stand against acts that endangered innocent lives and undermined regional stability.

“Pakistan will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, resolute in its commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, security and defence,” the Foreign Office said.

The Foreign Office statement came days after Islamabad, Riyadh and Ankara agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.

The three nations took the decision at an emergency meeting of the MJDA in Riyadh, the Foreign Office said on October 6, adding that it would be carried out under "approved arrangements" and the national laws of the three countries.

Later that day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif confirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye have been providing support to Saudi Arabia in its operations against Houthis in Yemen.

— With additional input from Reuters

headline: 12 terrorists, Afghan Taliban personnel killed as security forces foil infiltration bid in Kurram
subheadline: Soldier embraces martyrdom during intense exchange of fire with Indian-sponsored terrorists, says ISPR
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Naib Subedar Aman embraces martyrdom in intense border firefight.
ISPR says sanitisation operation targets remaining khwarij.
Afghan Taliban regime facilitating cross-border terrorism: ISPR

A soldier was martyred while 12 Fitna al-Khawarij and Afghan Taliban personnel were killed during an attempted infiltration from Afghanistan into Kurram district, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday.

The movement of a group of khwarij attempting to approach the international border from Afghanistan was detected on October 10, following which security forces effectively engaged them, the military's media wing said in a statement issued on October 11.

Despite maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, security forces faced firing from Afghan Taliban posts, which opened fire to support the infiltration attempt, the ISPR said.

It added that skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khwarij and Afghan Taliban personnel.

However, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, 40, a resident of Ghizer district, embraced martyrdom during the intense exchange of fire.

The ISPR said the incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border once again vindicated Pakistan's stance regarding the Afghan Taliban regime's failure to prevent terrorist organisations from using Afghan soil, alleging that the regime instead facilitated and patronised cross-border terrorism.

The military's media wing added that the Afghan Taliban regime had consistently failed to fulfil its international counter-terrorism obligations.

A sanitisation operation is under way in the area to eliminate any remaining Indian-sponsored khwarij, the statement said.

Reaffirming its commitment to defending the country's frontiers, the ISPR said security forces and law enforcement agencies would continue their counter-terrorism campaign under the "Azm-e-Istehkam" vision, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, to eliminate foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

The statement said the sacrifices of security personnel further reinforced Pakistan's commitment to safeguarding the nation and its frontiers at all costs.

The development comes two days after forces killed seven Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district.

The IBO was carried out against India-backed militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, with several hideouts also destroyed, the ISPR said.

Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021.

Pakistan recorded its highest monthly number of militant attacks in 12 years during September 2026.

According to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring anti-state violence in the region, 225 militant attacks were recorded across the country in September, compared with 199 in August — an increase of 13%. Militant attacks increased for the third consecutive month.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.

Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban authorities have failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.

Despite multiple rounds of talks, Islamabad and Kabul have yet to resolve their differences, with the issue of militant groups operating from Afghan soil remaining a major point of contention between the two sides.

headline: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as President Zardari approves summary on cabinet's advice
subheadline: Centre cites shortcomings in KP govt's counterterrorism efforts amid worsening security situation in province
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Federal cabinet cites security concerns and failed talks.
Governor Kundi to lead 11-member advisory council.
Arrangement to remain in place for six months: law minister.

President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday proclaimed an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, citing the province's worsening security situation.

"The President approved and signed the summary upon the Prime Minister's advice under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan," the President Secretariat's Media Wing said in a press release.

The decision followed recommendations from the federal cabinet, formal advice from the prime minister and law-and-order reports submitted by relevant security institutions.

The statement also cited the breakdown of negotiations between the government delegation and the provincial leadership over the deteriorating security situation.

The Centre had alleged shortcomings in the provincial government's counterterrorism efforts as grounds for the decision.

The Constitution allows the federal government to make provisions during an emergency, including suspending some constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies or authorities.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad that KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi would take charge with the assistance of an 11-member advisory council. He said the arrangement would initially remain in place for six months.

The development comes amid heightened political tensions following a long march led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

The march began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed to reach an agreement.

The talks broke down over disagreements concerning counterterrorism cooperation in KP and access to incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, including a meeting with his personal doctor.

The government and opposition traded accusations over the failure to reach an agreement as Afridi continued leading the march through the province.

Governor backs emergency in KP

Following the move, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Sunday that the province's people welcomed the presidential proclamation, adding that they wanted peace, stability, development and prosperity rather than unrest and insecurity.

In a video message addressed to KP residents, Kundi said the province's peace-loving people did not support terrorism or violent activities.

He said they had resolved not to support Fitna al-Khawarij and would stand shoulder to shoulder with security forces in the fight against terrorists until their last breath.

The governor said residents wanted a peaceful and prosperous future, with brotherly relations and mutual cooperation with other provinces.

He urged them to maintain peace and refrain from violating the law, inciting violence or engaging in rioting, warning that action would be taken against those who disturbed law and order or took the law into their own hands.

Fazlur Rehman terms act 'attack on democracy'

Separately, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has termed the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule an "attack on democracy", saying his party will reach out to the public and continue playing its role both inside and outside parliament.

Addressing a press conference, Fazlur Rehman said the government wanted the announcement of an end to the long march before accepting the protesters’ demands.

He said PTI had demanded permission to meet the party’s founder, Imran Khan.

The JUI-F chief said he had held discussions with Sohail Afridi, Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Shahram Khan Tarakai and Asad Qaiser regarding the situation.

According to Fazlur Rehman, PTI representatives had said they were ready to call off the long march if their demands were accepted.

Army deployed to assist administration

The federal government has also approved the deployment of the Pakistan Army in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Article 245 of the Constitution, according to a notification.

The army will assist the administration, protect citizens’ lives and safeguard public property and government installations. The deployment will remain in place for the duration of the emergency imposed on October 11.

The KP governor will determine the number of troops in consultation with GHQ and the Military Operations Directorate, the notification said.

headline: Ministers defend KP emergency as choice between 'daily martyrdoms', tough decision
subheadline: Info Minister Attaullah Tarar accuses PTI KP govt of having a "nexus" with terrorists
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Law Minister Tarar says terror incidents in province rose 196%.
Ministers cite worsening security behind emergency decision.
Naqvi says PTI negotiations continued until midnight.

ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Sunday defended the imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying the government faced a choice between witnessing daily martyrdoms or taking a “difficult decision”.

“We had two options: either we witness martyrdoms on a daily basis or take a difficult decision,” Naqvi told a press conference in Islamabad alongside Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Naqvi said the decision had been taken against the backdrop of the security situation in the province, maintaining that the federal government had tried for more than a month to bring the KP government on board in the fight against terrorism.

“Today was not an easy day for us,” the interior minister said, adding that he had personally remained in contact with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)-led provincial government behind the scenes.

“Our objective was to bring them on board so that we could fight the war against terrorism together,” he added.

Naqvi said the federal government had no issue with the PTI’s sit-in, maintaining that it could deal with the protest.

“Our issue is terrorism,” he said.

The interior minister said the government remained in contact with PTI leaders until around 11:45pm and sought their response on proposed changes to a draft.

“I called them at around 11:45pm and asked them to respond so that this situation could be avoided,” he said.

Naqvi said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also met Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman as part of the efforts, but no response was received.

He said the government had earlier held two days of negotiations with the PTI, during which Asad Qaiser had made it clear that his party would cooperate in the fight against terrorism.

According to Naqvi, the draft under discussion was changed three times and revised for a fourth time at the PTI’s request.

“When the fourth draft was finalised, they backed out,” he claimed.

Naqvi said he had also held several meetings with Sohail Afridi, maintaining that terrorism was the only subject discussed during those interactions and that no political matters were taken up.

He said it had been agreed four months ago to enhance police capacity in five districts, with the federal government offering to address a shortage of funds raised by Afridi.

The interior minister claimed that during the first round of negotiations, the provincial side had agreed to the imposition of emergency in 12 districts.

Naqvi said the security situation in those districts was “very bad”, questioning how the PTI had nevertheless taken its long march through the affected areas.

The interior minister maintained that the government’s position was clear that terrorism had nothing to do with politics.

Terror incidents increased 196%: Tarar

Speaking on the occasion, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said terrorism incidents in KP had increased by 196%, describing the figure as the “most alarming” aspect of the situation.

He said terrorism had become a routine occurrence in the province and accused the provincial government of pursuing its politics while neglecting the protection of the public.

Tarar said the federal cabinet decided to impose the emergency after considering the circumstances in the province, adding that the KP governor had also conveyed “very concerning” developments to the federal government.

“Such steps are not taken happily,” the law minister said, maintaining that emergency powers should be exercised in the interest of national security and the country.

Tarar said the president had acted within the Constitution by exercising powers provided under Articles 232 and 234.

He said the provincial government had ceased to function under the emergency, with the governor empowered to administer the province under the federation.

The law minister added that the governor would be assisted by an 11-member advisory council, while a separate secretariat had been established for 12 districts severely affected by terrorism.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, meanwhile, accused the former provincial government of having a “nexus” with terrorists and alleged that it had effectively “outsourced” some districts to them.

He claimed there was “irrefutable evidence” that the provincial government was pushing KP towards destruction.

The information minister said the advisory council would comprise technocrats, including Lt Gen (retd) Nigar Johar, Kifayatullah Khan, Tariq Mahmood Pasha, Aamir Javed, Dr Aamir Abdullah, Dr Sarfaraz Ali Shah, Dr Muhammad Irshad, Asif Rafiq Afridi, Tayyab Qureshi, Usman Saifullah Khan and Samar Haroon Bilour.

headline: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as president approves cabinet decision
description: Federal cabinet notes "provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism"; PTI condemns move, says peace cannot be established by "weakening provincial autonomy".
author: Syed Irfan Raza, News Desk
article_text:
Key developments:

Emergency imposed under Article 232, governor’s rule under Article 234
Cabinet recommended move due to KP govt’s ‘deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’
Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam appointed as KP chief secretary
PTI’s Gohar condemns decision as undemocratic, says peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy
Governor Kundi calls for unity for ‘new chapter’ in KP’s development

ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet.

The measures have been approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the President House said in a statement. The two provisions pertain to the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule.

Following the imposition, internet disruptions were being reported from parts of Peshawar, with Dawn unable to contact its correspondents there. Earlier in the day, massive police deployment and increased barriers on certain routes using containers were witnessed in the city.

According to sources in the telecom sector, mobile network and data services have been slowed or shut down in selected areas of some cities. However, there is no province-wide shutdown of mobile data or internet.

The decision to impose the provisions came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in KP.

A statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.

The members proposed, given the “gravity” of the situation, that the PM advise the president to exercise “his constitutional authority and impose an emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution”.

A couple of hours after the decision was announced, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on the PTI’s long march, claimed that the KP CM had been taken into custody.

Dawn has reached out to police for a comment.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

It may be recalled that in July 2024, when Afridi’s predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur was the chief minister, the KP Assembly passed a resolution urging the federal government to consult with it and the provincial government before launching a new military operation.

The resolution, passed by a majority vote, cautioned that proceeding without provincial consent could hinder the offensive’s success and result in adverse consequences, for which the federal government would be responsible.

In December that year, the assembly voted unanimously against a potential military operation in parts of Khyber and Bannu districts.

About a year later, after Afridi became the KP CM, the provincial assembly convened a grand jirga with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and other parties in attendance. The moot unanimously demanded that the Centre prioritise negotiations with Afghanistan and consult the KP government over Afghan policy.

Constitutional provisions

Emergency

Article 232 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of emergency in a province.

It says, “If the president is satisfied that a grave emergency exists in which the security of Pakistan, or any part thereof, is threatened by war or external aggression, or by internal disturbance beyond the power of a provincial government to control, he may issue a Proclamation of Emergency.”

However, invoking this article “due to internal disturbances beyond the powers of a provincial government to control” requires a resolution from the provincial assembly of that province.

In case the president “acts on his own” — which is not currently the case — the Proclamation of Emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days.

According to this provision, parliament “shall have power to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during the time of the proclamation of an emergency.

Nothing in this Article shall restrict the power of a provincial assembly to make any law which the Constitution empowers it to make, but if any provision of a provincial law is repugnant to any provision of an Act by Parliament, the latter would prevail and the provincial law would be void as long as the parliamentary Act is in effect.

Governor’s rule

On the other hand, Article 234 deals with the imposition of the governor’s rule “in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province”. For imposition of the governor’s rule, the president simply requires a request from the provincial governor, it says.

“A proclamation issued under this Article shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time,” the Constitution reads.

However, it adds that no such proclamation shall in any case remain in force for more than six months.

Article 233, which provides powers to the president to suspend certain fundamental rights during the emergency period, was not mentioned in the summary signed by President Zardari.

Chief secretary appointed

Following the approval, the federal government appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the chief secretary of KP, according to an official notification, a copy of which is available with Dawn.

The appointment will take effect immediately and remain in place until further orders, it said.

Dr Irfan, a Grade 22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was previously serving as secretary of the Power Division in the federal Ministry of Energy. He hails from Mardan.

In a separate notification, the federal government also placed Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada at the disposal of the KP government with “immediate effect and until further orders”.

Akhunzada, a Grade 20 PAS officer, was serving as an additional secretary at PMO.

He hails from Charsadda and has also served as additional political agent for North and South Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in KP, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan.

‘Peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy’

PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan strongly condemned the imposition of emergency in KP and “completely rejected” it.

“This is an extremely alarming and grave political mistake and an undemocratic measure — the people will never accept such actions against their rights,” Gohar wrote in a post on X.

He stated: “There is still time; this decision can be withdrawn in a few days. Let the federation set aside its ego, understand the ground realities, accept legitimate demands, respect the sentiments and emotions of the people, and save the country from further political and economic damage and from pushing back the democratic process.

“Revisiting political decisions is not a sign of weakness but of wisdom in the national interest — otherwise, great damage will be done.”

Stressing that the mandate of the people of KP was their constitutional and legal right, the PTI chairman said: “Peace cannot be established, nor stability brought, by ignoring this mandate, weakening provincial autonomy, and creating conflict between the federation and the province.”

He asserted that there was “no disagreement on eliminating terrorism, but the fight against terrorism cannot be used as a justification to suppress the people’s voice, achieve political objectives, or limit the province’s constitutional authority”.

“Terrorism can only be combated through national unity and a joint strategy,” Gohar maintained.

“The federation cannot be strengthened by weakening the provinces. The solution to problems lies not in force, confrontation, and extraordinary measures, but in political wisdom, supremacy of the Constitution, and meaningful negotiations and practical steps.”

The PTI chairman said his party will raise the matter on “every constitutional, legal, and democratic forum for the protection of the people’s mandate, provincial autonomy, and constitutional and democratic rights”.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn that the party has called a meeting of the parliamentary committee to mull three options as a counterstrategy.

“We will discuss challenging the decision in the court, boycotting the National Assembly, Senate and proceedings in provincial assemblies,” he said. Peaceful protests across the country were also under consideration.

However, he said that the final decision will be taken by the PTI’s political committee.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), of which PTI is a part, termed the move a violation of the Constitution.

In a statement, the opposition alliance particularly assailed President Zardari’s PPP, claiming that the “most undemocratic actions and the imposition of governor’s rule” had been the hallmark of the party in the country’s history.

“On the one hand, despite the extremely dire administrative and law and order situation in Balochistan, no such step has been taken, while on the other hand, this province — whose assembly and government stand on the true and real mandate of the people — has been targeted,” it contended.

TTAP said it would convene a meeting on the matter and announce a joint course of action.

Separately, the PTI parliamentary committee held a meeting and categorically rejected the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP. In a statement, it termed the development “a direct assault on the public mandate and an unacceptable move”.

“In a three-hour-long meeting of the PTI parliamentary party, the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was strongly condemned and unanimously rejected. The meeting declared this step contrary to facts, unconstitutional, undemocratic, and a blatant insult to the public mandate of the province,” the statement said.

“The parliamentary party made it clear that measures to render the elected provincial government ineffective and usurp its constitutional powers could pose grave threats to the federal system and democratic traditions. Such decisions will increase political instability and public unrest in the province, while already existing tensions between the federation and the province will further intensify,” it added.

The statement added that the solution to political differences should be found through constitutional and democratic procedures and mutual consultation, rather than through force and coercion.

It also raised serious questions regarding the conduct of the federal government.

“The parliamentary party took the stance that if terrorism and the deteriorating law and order situation are the primary justification for the imposition of emergency, then why is the situation in Balochistan being ignored?” the statement asked.

The meeting also made it clear that Afridi was the elected chief minister a member of the provincial assembly.

“Measures regarding his arrest, detention, or the usurping of his constitutional and democratic powers were strongly condemned. The meeting termed such actions an insult to the public mandate and a dangerous precedent for democratic traditions,” it said.

Governor Kundi urges unity for ‘new chapter’

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi said the decision was made for “establishing peace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the prosperity of its people, and the development of the province”.

“I am your governor, but beyond that, I want to play my role as a servant of this soil and a protector of your rights. Let us come together to bring peace to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and begin a new chapter of our province’s development,” he said in a statement.

Kundi assured the public that it was his responsibility to raise their issues on the relevant forums.

Recalling the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism, he said, “Now the time has come that we do not let these sacrifices go to waste and together establish lasting peace in our province.”

The PPP leader urged the public to set aside their political differences and unite for the province’s peace, the protection of its people, and the future of the coming generations.

“We must not let our differences become an obstacle in the path of our province’s common interests.”

Cannot allow PTI to destabilise the economy: PM tells cabinet

Addressing the cabinet meeting, the premier said the PTI-led KP government cannot be allowed to derail the stabilising economy amid tensions between the two sides.

“I will not allow them (PTI) to destabilise the economy,” he said during the meeting.

On terrorism in KP and Balochistan, the premier said, “The way common citizens are being martyred, the way police officials and security officials, children and mothers [..] there can be nothing more heart-wrenching.”

He recalled that Pakistan has repeatedly urged neighbouring Afghanistan to rein in the terrorist elements; however, “they still do not understand it”.

PM Shehbaz also reiterated his condemnation of the recent deadly Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, noting the long-standing fraternal ties between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

“Our only goal is that peace should be restored in the region,” he said.

“Pakistan expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia and stands with it. We will not tolerate any aggression against Saudi Arabia,” he said, adding that it was a “red line” for Pakistan.

During his address, PM Shehbaz also spoke of the recent staff-level agreement reached with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

“It is hoped that we will unlock the $1.2 billion tranche within this year,” he said, recalling a meeting with the IMF’s Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last month.

He commended the political and military leadership for “working together day and night” in bringing fiscal discipline to Pakistan.

The premier recalled his visit to London last month, where he had met with senior executives from leading global financial institutions.

He also spoke of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the international community, taking note of the appreciation Pakistan has received for mediation in the Middle East conflict.

“Pakistan continues to play its role with hard work and sincerity,” he said, particularly lauding the role of the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

sentences.text: Key developments: Emergency imposed under Article 232, governor’s rule under Article 234 Cabinet recommended move due to KP govt’s ‘deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’ Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam appointed as KP chief secretary PTI’s Gohar condemns decision as undemocratic, says peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy Governor Kundi calls for unity for ‘new chapter’ in KP’s development ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet.
The measures have been approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the President House said in a statement.
The two provisions pertain to the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule.
Following the imposition, internet disruptions were being reported from parts of Peshawar, with Dawn unable to contact its correspondents there.
Earlier in the day, massive police deployment and increased barriers on certain routes using containers were witnessed in the city.
According to sources in the telecom sector, mobile network and data services have been slowed or shut down in selected areas of some cities.
However, there is no province-wide shutdown of mobile data or internet.
The decision to impose the provisions came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in KP.

A statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.

The members proposed, given the “gravity” of the situation, that the PM advise the president to exercise “his constitutional authority and impose an emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution”.

A couple of hours after the decision was announced, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on the PTI’s long march, claimed that the KP CM had been taken into custody.
Dawn has reached out to police for a comment.
The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.
That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre.
They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.
The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied.
It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.
On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

It may be recalled that in July 2024, when Afridi’s predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur was the chief minister, the KP Assembly passed a resolution urging the federal government to consult with it and the provincial government before launching a new military operation.

The resolution, passed by a majority vote, cautioned that proceeding without provincial consent could hinder the offensive’s success and result in adverse consequences, for which the federal government would be responsible.
In December that year, the assembly voted unanimously against a potential military operation in parts of Khyber and Bannu districts.
About a year later, after Afridi became the KP CM, the provincial assembly convened a grand jirga with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and other parties in attendance.
The moot unanimously demanded that the Centre prioritise negotiations with Afghanistan and consult the KP government over Afghan policy.
Constitutional provisions Emergency Article 232 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of emergency in a province.

It says, “If the president is satisfied that a grave emergency exists in which the security of Pakistan, or any part thereof, is threatened by war or external aggression, or by internal disturbance beyond the power of a provincial government to control, he may issue a Proclamation of Emergency.
However, invoking this article “due to internal disturbances beyond the powers of a provincial government to control” requires a resolution from the provincial assembly of that province.
In case the president “acts on his own” — which is not currently the case — the Proclamation of Emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days.

According to this provision, parliament “shall have power to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during the time of the proclamation of an emergency.

Nothing in this Article shall restrict the power of a provincial assembly to make any law which the Constitution empowers it to make, but if any provision of a provincial law is repugnant to any provision of an Act by Parliament, the latter would prevail and the provincial law would be void as long as the parliamentary Act is in effect.
Governor’s rule On the other hand, Article 234 deals with the imposition of the governor’s rule “in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province”.
For imposition of the governor’s rule, the president simply requires a request from the provincial governor, it says.

“A proclamation issued under this Article shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time,” the Constitution reads.
However, it adds that no such proclamation shall in any case remain in force for more than six months.
Article 233, which provides powers to the president to suspend certain fundamental rights during the emergency period, was not mentioned in the summary signed by President Zardari.

Chief secretary appointed Following the approval, the federal government appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the chief secretary of KP, according to an official notification, a copy of which is available with Dawn.
The appointment will take effect immediately and remain in place until further orders, it said.
Dr Irfan, a Grade 22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was previously serving as secretary of the Power Division in the federal Ministry of Energy.
He hails from Mardan.
In a separate notification, the federal government also placed Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada at the disposal of the KP government with “immediate effect and until further orders”.
Akhunzada, a Grade 20 PAS officer, was serving as an additional secretary at PMO.
He hails from Charsadda and has also served as additional political agent for North and South Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in KP, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan.
‘Peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy’ PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan strongly condemned the imposition of emergency in KP and “completely rejected” it.
“This is an extremely alarming and grave political mistake and an undemocratic measure — the people will never accept such actions against their rights,” Gohar wrote in a post on X.
He stated: “There is still time; this decision can be withdrawn in a few days.

Let the federation set aside its ego, understand the ground realities, accept legitimate demands, respect the sentiments and emotions of the people, and save the country from further political and economic damage and from pushing back the democratic process.
“Revisiting political decisions is not a sign of weakness but of wisdom in the national interest — otherwise, great damage will be done.

Stressing that the mandate of the people of KP was their constitutional and legal right, the PTI chairman said: “Peace cannot be established, nor stability brought, by ignoring this mandate, weakening provincial autonomy, and creating conflict between the federation and the province.

He asserted that there was “no disagreement on eliminating terrorism, but the fight against terrorism cannot be used as a justification to suppress the people’s voice, achieve political objectives, or limit the province’s constitutional authority”.
“Terrorism can only be combated through national unity and a joint strategy,” Gohar maintained.
“The federation cannot be strengthened by weakening the provinces.
The solution to problems lies not in force, confrontation, and extraordinary measures, but in political wisdom, supremacy of the Constitution, and meaningful negotiations and practical steps.

The PTI chairman said his party will raise the matter on “every constitutional, legal, and democratic forum for the protection of the people’s mandate, provincial autonomy, and constitutional and democratic rights”.
PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn that the party has called a meeting of the parliamentary committee to mull three options as a counterstrategy.
“We will discuss challenging the decision in the court, boycotting the National Assembly, Senate and proceedings in provincial assemblies,” he said.
Peaceful protests across the country were also under consideration.
However, he said that the final decision will be taken by the PTI’s political committee.
The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), of which PTI is a part, termed the move a violation of the Constitution.

In a statement, the opposition alliance particularly assailed President Zardari’s PPP, claiming that the “most undemocratic actions and the imposition of governor’s rule” had been the hallmark of the party in the country’s history.

“On the one hand, despite the extremely dire administrative and law and order situation in Balochistan, no such step has been taken, while on the other hand, this province — whose assembly and government stand on the true and real mandate of the people — has been targeted,” it contended.
TTAP said it would convene a meeting on the matter and announce a joint course of action.

It also raised serious questions regarding the conduct of the federal government.

Let us come together to bring peace to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and begin a new chapter of our province’s development,” he said in a statement.
Kundi assured the public that it was his responsibility to raise their issues on the relevant forums.
Recalling the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism, he said, “Now the time has come that we do not let these sacrifices go to waste and together establish lasting peace in our province.
The PPP leader urged the public to set aside their political differences and unite for the province’s peace, the protection of its people, and the future of the coming generations.
“We must not let our differences become an obstacle in the path of our province’s common interests.

He recalled that Pakistan has repeatedly urged neighbouring Afghanistan to rein in the terrorist elements; however, “they still do not understand it”.

headline: Intercity transport suspended in Lahore, bus terminals reportedly sealed
description: Major private bus operators, including Faisal Movers and Daewoo, suspend services amid reported restrictions on public transport.
author: Imran Gabol
article_text:
LAHORE: Intercity bus services from Lahore to several destinations across the country were suspended on Sunday after the administration reportedly sealed all general bus terminals in the city late on Saturday night, leaving passengers stranded and disrupting travel.

The closures affected passengers travelling to Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh, southern Punjab and other parts of central Punjab. Several passengers reported difficulties after their tickets were cancelled and transport services suspended.

Meanwhile, major private bus operators, including Faisal Movers and Daewoo, suspended their services amid reports of restrictions on public transport movement on motorways and national highways.

Representatives of Faisal Movers and Daewoo told Dawn that their services had been suspended and buses were not being dispatched due to the restrictions.

However, motorway police spokesperson Imran Shah told Dawn that motorways and highways were open to traffic and that he was unaware of any directions to suspend bus services.

Another motorway police official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said buses were not operating on motorways or highways because of the PTI’s protest call. He added that people travelling in private vehicles could use the roads.

Punjab Transport Department Secretary Imran Sikandar Baloch was unavailable for comment despite repeated attempts to contact him on his mobile phone.

The development comes as the PTI launched its march on October 4 despite warnings from the Centre.

So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

A day earlier, containers were transported to Swabi Interchange — where the PTI had called on its workers to gather — as well as the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.

headline: Pakistan Army deployed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in aid of civil power
description: Shipping containers placed in Peshawar; police reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House.
author: Umer Farooq, Ismail Khan, Ikram Junaidi, Iftikhar A. Khan, Manzoor Ali
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after imposing an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

The authorisation of the army deployment was made through Statutory Regulatory Order, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday.

According to the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the “safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations” in the province.

The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added.

Copies of the order were forwarded to the president’s secretary, prime minister’s adviser, the KP governor’s secretary, the Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, the KP home secretary, the inspector general of police (IGP) in the province, the Peshawar High Court registrar and other officials.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Shipping containers block roads

Shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block roads after the imposition of the emergency.

Containers were placed near Peshawar’s railway station to block the routes towards Khyber Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and beyond. They were also placed near Edwardes College to block entry to Jail Road and Malik Saad Shaheed Flyover, while people were turned away from Sher Shah Suri Road as it was reported to be completely closed.

Police were reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House. The deployment included personnel called from other districts.

Police and personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including many in plainclothes, were seen patrolling the roads leading to Governor House, the central police office, Peshawar police headquarters and other government installations largely located in the Red Zone, a correspondent reported.

Vehicles with tinted glasses, police mobile vans, armored personnel carriers and other LEA vehicles were reportedly the only transport visible in and around the cantonment area, with life at a standstill and the area appearing deserted.

Another correspondent reported that the road leading to Khyber Road was shuttered by a container and the traffic control gate closed. A large number of police personnel were also seen around Surey Pul, a favoured spot for protesters.

Grand Trunk (GT) Road was blocked by containers at Firdous Chowk and the correspondent reported a large number of police personnel in the area. Only pedestrians were allowed to move ahead.

Additionally, containers near Bala Hisar Fort and outside the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) office on Arbab Road blocked entry towards Mall Road.

Only official vehicles were being allowed to travel from Governor House towards the Chief Minister’s House, while tight security was reported on Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum road where they are located. The Civil Secretariat was seen to be deserted.

Royal Artillery (RA) Bazaar has been closed, while Saddar remains partially open.

Additionally, Peshawar’s Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) stations were reported to be shuttered by Dawn’s correspondent.

The stretch of Khyber Road connecting to University Road and Airport Road at Aman Chowk was reported to be open but with low traffic. A large police contingent was seen at Aman Chowk. Meanwhile, University Road was blocked by containers at Tehkal, and containers at Stadium Chowk allowed for only single-file passage of vehicles on both sides.

Earlier, traffic jams were reported due to the closure of Khyber Road, which connects GT Road with the eastern side of University Road and serves as the main artery and choke point. The resulting diversions created pressure on auxiliary roads.

The area is part of the cantonment, and the Red Zone contains important installations such as the Corps Commander’s House, civil secretariat, central police office, CM Secretariat, CM House and Governor House.

All telecoms services, including landline and DSL, are reported to be suspended in the provincial capital. The city had witnessed a nearly 48-hour mobile service blackout just days ago, on account of the presence of the PTI in the city for its long march.

With networks suspended, people faced immense issues in withdrawing money from bank accounts, as ATMs remained out of service for the entire day.

Aside from the suspension of cellular network and broadband services, however, the situation remained normal for those living on Kohat Road, Charsadda Road, GT Road beyond Pir Zakorhi Bridge, and the area bordering the Khyber district, as well as others on the outskirts of the provincial capital. Vehicles of the armed forces were also reported to be patrolling cantonment areas and a heavy deployment of police was reported in both the city and its outskirts including Kohat Road, GT Road, University Road and Warsak Road.

On Saturday, KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed put district police on alert for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force.

A notification issued by the IGP’s office directed not only officers in Peshawar but also district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and even station house officers (SHOs) to personally monitor the situation.

It said DPOs could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action.

It added that the use of force was to be carried out on a gradated basis, noting that in the first phase, protesters should be clearly warned against violence before police began to use forceful measures.

KP House sealed, NPC refuses to allow TTAP presser

In Islamabad, the main opposition alliance — which would typically hold pressers at KP House — could not find a place to hold a press conference in the urban areas as KP House was sealed.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) has therefore decided to hold its presser at Jamia Al Wilaya near Bhara Kahu on the Murree Expressway.

Speaking to Dawn, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed.

He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee.

“Now we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.

headline: Soldier martyred, 12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram: ISPR
description: Afghan Taliban posts opened fire to support the infiltration attempt, army's media wing says.
author: News Desk
article_text:
A soldier was martyred and 12 terrorists killed in an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram district, the army’s media wing said on Sunday.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that the movement of a group of khawarij attempting to cross the international border from Afghanistan into Pakistan was detected in Kurram district on Sunday, where security forces engaged them effectively.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

Security forces, “maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, effectively thwarted the infiltration attempt”, the statement added.

It further said that Afghan Taliban posts had also opened fire to support the infiltration attempt by the khawarij.

“The skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khawarij and Afghan Taliban,” the statement said. During the exchange of fire, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman was martyred after “fighting gallantly”.

This incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border vindicates Islamabad’s “objective and factual stance regarding the willful abject failure of the Afghan Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil to the terrorist organisation”, the statement added.

“The security forces of Pakistan remain resolute and unwavering in their commitment to defend the nation’s frontiers,” said the ISPR, adding that sanitisation operation is being conducted in the area to eliminate any other Indian sponsored khawariji found in the area.”

“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision Azm-i-Istehkam as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.”

“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation and its frontiers at all costs,” it said.

In a statement on X, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for “foiling the infiltration attempt”.

He expressed “heartfelt condolences and expression of sympathy” to the bereaved family of the martyred Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, adding that nation takes pride in the “professional capabilities and courage” of the security forces.

KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time

September particularly witnessed a significant deterioration in Pakistan’s overall security environment, accompanied by growing political, economic and regional pressures, according to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

Terrorist violence increased substantially, with 225 attacks recorded nationwide, compared with 199 in August, representing a 13.1 per cent increase and the highest monthly total recorded in 12 years.

On Sept 27, 14 people, including two rescue officials, were martyred and 35 sustained injuries after a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into a police checkpost in and then targeted an ambulance taking bodies to hospital in DI Khan.

On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation.

headline: 'Our fight is against terrorism': Kundi chairs first meeting of KP Advisory Council
description: Tells council members first order of business is the law and order situation, and there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces.
author: News Desk
article_text:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday chaired the first meeting of the KP Advisory Council, which was formed by the federal government following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

At the outset of the meeting, all members of the council introduced themselves and their portfolios.

Addressing the meeting, Kundi congratulated the members of the council, while noting that they would have to face many challenges. He said that they would get a briefing on the portfolios they had been assigned and would get a few days to familiarise themselves.

“We have to fast-track things. There will be zero tolerance on corruption. Things should be done in a timely manner,” he said, adding that they would have to demonstrate a clear difference from the work done by their predecessors.

He said that the first order of business was the law and order situation, adding that there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces.

He said that the current situation was an “opportunity” as he called for building the province’s soft image.

“If we have peace, we will get tourists and investors. My support is with you. I am available for you 24/7,” he said.

Kundi then went on to read out a message for the people of the province, in which he said that due to “extraordinary circumstances”, “necessary measures” were taken under the Constitution.

He said that he would refrain from levelling allegations and political rhetoric.

“I have one message: peace, protection and stability have to be brought back to KP,” he said. He added that the people of KP had paid a huge price for the terrorism that plagued the province.

“The time has now come to give the people of the province, who have rendered these sacrifices, the right to peace. Our fight is against terrorism. Our fight is against the ideology and network which facilitates terrorism and weakens the implementation of the law,” he said.

He also said that Pakhtuns were not a cause of terrorism, but were the “biggest victims”. Therefore, the state had resolved that terrorism would be eliminated from KP and the people would be allowed to live their lives without fear.

“My first priority will be protecting the peace and the people. Right now, our biggest priority is taking effective steps against terrorism. For this, the capacity of the police and the Counter Terrorism Department will be increased,” he said.

He went on to say that another objective would be to cater to the people.

“Mere statements are not the real test of a government, rather the service it provides to the people,” he said. Kundi said that the council would focus on healthcare, education and employment.

The last objective, he said, would be to eliminate the whole ecosystem giving rise to terrorism in the province.

“We cannot solve the issue by just targeting terrorists. Those facilitating and financing … must be eliminated,” he said, adding that those involved in terrorism would be dealt with according to the law.

He assured the people of KP that the “extraordinary steps” taken were not meant to target a particular party or group. Kundi said that the main purpose was to ensure peace and security as he asked for their cooperation.
